akr_airfield.text: RAF Akrotiri Movements. Say the word and the Airbridge takes you home to Brize Norton.

c_brineling.text: It stands on one leg and stares at you with a look of deep and total calm. It has been doing this since before breakfast.

c_brineflame.text: A flame-pink flamingo at the heart of the lake, glowing like the sunset. It looks at you the way a very important person looks at a waiter.

akr_cypriot.text: I'm Cypriot, and I live in a village inside the Base Area. The British have the bases, and the Republic of Cyprus has the rest, and the villages in between all get on with their lives.
Everyone has a cousin on the other side of the fence. Nobody minds. Coffee is coffee.

akr_kafe.text: Cypriot coffee, boiled in a little pot and served with the grounds still in. Never stir it, and never drink the last sip.
Order it metrios, medium sweet. Or sketos, no sugar. Or glykos, which is sugar with a bit of coffee.

akr_flight.text: I've flown to Akrotiri more times than I can count. It's the last decent stop before the Gulf, and the first on the way home.
The runway is long, the sea is warm, and the tea, I'm told, is passable.

akr_diver.text: The water off Akrotiri is clear as a bell. You can see sixty feet down on a calm day, to the sand and the old pottery.
The coast has a lot of old shipwrecks and a lot of amphora fragments. Take only photographs and leave only bubbles.

akr_archaeologist.text: Look at the stage. The sea behind it isn't an accident: the Greeks liked a view. They built a theatre to be seen against the horizon.
Earthquakes took Kourion in the 4th century, and the rest we've dug up with trowels and a lot of patience.

akr_monk.text: I look after the cats. There are about thirty of them at the moment, and they have never once listened to me.
The legend says the monastery was founded to house the cats that Saint Helena sent. I say they came to us, and we've just never made them leave.

akr_ranger.text: In summer I walk the beach at night with a red torch. The turtles hate white light.
If you find a nest, mark it and tell me. Don't touch it. The baby turtles know what they're doing.

akrotiri_bureau.text: Welcome to the bureau de change. Local money in, sterling out, or the other way round. A small fee, and a very small queue.
